review.verdict: The calm-robot-vs-chaotic-human contrast reads, but a disconnected floating suitcase, an illegible toppled-shelf 'building', an overlapping gear, a sparse top half, and a composition that closely echoes a recent blueprint-grid slopper keep this from publish quality.
revisionNotes: Suitcase: reattach to the human's hand (side: right, offset near [40, 10]) or switch pose to a carry stance; right now it floats alone near the divider with no visible connection to the body.
Building: swap the server-rack 'datacenter' stand-in for a recognizable office/building silhouette (door, window, roofline) so it reads as a toppled company rather than a broken shelf.
Nameplate: scale it up (0.8 → 1.1) and increase contrast/line weight so the 'knocked askew' sign is legible instead of reading as a stray rod.
Gear: shift it further along the belt, clear of the robot's leg, so it doesn't overlap the body and reads as a separate object rolling off the line.
Composition: raise the ground anchors (y ~0.78 → ~0.65) or add detail to the upper half; the top half of the square is empty and the scene feels bottom-heavy.

Novelty: this blueprint-grid + vertical divider + chart/building/human-left, robot-right template closely repeats at least one recent slopper — try a different palette, split direction, or drop the divider for a single continuous scene.

review.verdict: Reads as "something collapsed, something else calmly continues" with correct human/robot casting, but the composition leaves nearly a third of the canvas empty, drops the brief's dividing line, and strands the suitcase and chart as disconnected props; it's also too close to a recent blueprint-grid piece. Average ~3.1 — below the 3.5 bar, does not pass.
revisionNotes: Composition: the bottom ~30% of the canvas is empty grid; recenter/scale the group (or drop chart down, raise belt) so elements span the full square instead of hugging the top half.

Add the thin vertical dividing line called for in the brief between the building/human side and the robot side — right now nothing visually separates 'chaos' from 'calm', so the split-screen joke doesn't read.

Suitcase prop floats disconnected in open space between the human and robot (scale 0.5, offset 40,10 off the human's hand); reattach it directly at the hand anchor and bump to ~0.7 scale so it reads as carried, not stray.

Chart is floating top-center, disconnected from the building it's supposed to sit beside ('at its feet' per brief); move it down next to the building's base so the left side reads as one beat, not three separate islands.

Novelty: this building + falling chart + person + robot blueprint-grid layout is close to the recent 'Business As Usual' slopper — vary the background treatment or building silhouette to differentiate.
Building reads as a pitched-roof house, not an office; flatten the roofline or add a flat top/signage cue so 'company building' is legible at a glance.

review.verdict: Casting and metaphor are sound (human exec vs. calm robot), but a disconnected floating suitcase, an ambiguous toppled-sign shape, a top-heavy empty canvas, and a composition that closely echoes other recent blueprint split-divider pieces pull the average below the bar.
revisionNotes: Suitcase floats disconnected near the divider instead of reading as held; attach it to the human's hand side with a tighter offset and scale it up to ~0.9 so the 'walking out with suitcase' beat is legible.

The toppled-nameplate shape overlaps the leaning doorway and reads as a ramp or ladder, not a fallen sign; redraw it as a flat plank with a couple of text-line strokes, lying clear of the door on the ground.

Content is crammed into the bottom third while the top ~60% of the canvas is empty grid; raise the building/human/chart group and the robot/belt group toward mid-canvas (y ~0.55-0.6) or scale them up to use the square better.

This blueprint split-by-vertical-divider layout (chart left, human, robot right) is close to two other recent blueprint entries with the same structure; vary the composition (diagonal split, different grouping) or switch palette/style so it doesn't read as a repeat.
The gear on the conveyor is a generic 'new product' symbol and doesn't specifically evoke 'smarter chatbot'; add a small screen or chat-bubble accent on the gear so the launch reads more precisely.
